skill.name: chipsec
skill.description: Guide static UEFI and BIOS firmware analysis with Intel CHIPSEC. It covers offline threat scans, EFI inventories, baseline comparison, firmware decoding, NVRAM review, and SPI descriptor parsing.
skill.summary: Run offline CHIPSEC workflows for UEFI firmware security analysis.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily defensive documentation for offline CHIPSEC firmware analysis, and most static hits are Markdown command examples or threat terminology. The confirmed risk is repeated setup guidance that uses sudo and chmod 777 on a CHIPSEC package directory, which should be replaced before publication.

remediation.suggestion: Replace chmod 777 with a least-privilege directory owned by the current user, or configure CHIPSEC output to a user-controlled analysis directory.

remediation.issue: Elevated writes to package install paths
remediation.suggestion: Avoid sudo setup steps in the skill. If elevation is unavoidable, require explicit user review and explain the exact path and ownership change.
Update both the prerequisite and troubleshooting sections so they present the same safe logging configuration.

content.value_statement: Firmware teams need repeatable evidence when reviewing BIOS and UEFI images. This skill guides CHIPSEC scans, inventories, decoding, and baseline checks for offline firmware analysis.
actual_capabilities: Guides known UEFI threat scans with CHIPSEC blocklist modules.
Generates EFI executable inventories with hashes for baseline review.
Explains firmware decoding outputs, including volumes, EFI files, and NVRAM data.
Supports before-and-after firmware comparisons for update verification.
Provides troubleshooting steps for common CHIPSEC format and module errors.
Organizes incident response workflows for suspect firmware dumps.
limitations: Requires CHIPSEC and supporting tools to be installed separately.
Only covers offline firmware images, not live hardware assessment.
Some CHIPSEC outputs require expert firmware knowledge to interpret.
The setup guidance includes unsafe permission commands that need revision.

use_cases.title: Review Firmware Updates
use_cases.description: Compare original and updated firmware images to identify unexpected EFI module changes.

use_cases.title: Investigate Suspect Devices
use_cases.description: Run threat scans and inventory generation during firmware incident response.

use_cases.title: Document IoT Firmware
use_cases.description: Decode extracted firmware images and collect NVRAM and EFI module evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through an offline CHIPSEC threat scan for my UEFI firmware image.

prompt_templates.title: Create an EFI Inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me generate and interpret an EFI executable inventory for a firmware dump.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Firmware Versions
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a CHIPSEC workflow to compare a known-good firmware image with an updated image.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Incident Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me structure a firmware incident response report using CHIPSEC scan, inventory, decode, and NVRAM results.

output_examples.input: Scan a firmware image for known UEFI threats.
output_examples.output: A triage summary listing scan status, matched threat names, affected module identifiers, hashes, and recommended follow-up checks.

output_examples.input: Compare a firmware update against a baseline.
output_examples.output: A change summary that separates expected vendor updates from unknown EFI module additions or hash changes.

output_examples.input: Decode a firmware image and review NVRAM output.
output_examples.output: A review checklist covering decoded volumes, extracted EFI files, available NVRAM variables, and missing or encrypted regions.

best_practices: Work only with firmware images you own or are authorized to analyze.
Keep original firmware dumps read-only and store outputs in a separate analysis directory.
Validate CHIPSEC findings with manual review before reporting confirmed compromise.
anti_patterns: Do not run live hardware checks when you only intend offline analysis.
Do not apply broad writable permissions to system package directories.
Do not treat a clean blocklist scan as proof that firmware is safe.

faq.question: Does this skill require physical hardware access?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on offline analysis of firmware dump files.

faq.question: Can it detect every UEFI implant?
faq.answer: No. It checks known patterns and supports deeper review, but unknown implants may not match.

faq.question: What file types are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers common BIOS and UEFI image formats such as BIN, ROM, FD, CAP, FV, and flash dumps.

faq.question: Does it install CHIPSEC?
faq.answer: No. The user must install CHIPSEC and related tools separately.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code run these workflows?
faq.answer: They can guide the workflow and, with permission, run commands in an appropriate local environment.

faq.question: Is the current setup guidance safe?
faq.answer: Not fully. The audit found broad permission commands that should be replaced with least-privilege setup steps.
